item.title: Security Alert: Holiday Travel, November 13, 2026
item.content:encoded:
Security Alert: Holiday Travel, November 13, 2026

Location: Europewide

Event:  As the holiday season approaches, U.S. citizens should remain vigilant of their surroundings and practice sound personal security and situational awareness.  Large gatherings and public events may present a target of opportunity for terrorist groups and criminals.  Terrorists – including lone actors – may attack with little or no warning, targeting tourist locations such as markets, transportation hubs, shopping malls, place of worship, and other public areas.

U.S. citizens should exercise extra vigilance at holiday festivals and events and other locations with large crowds.  Visitors to congested and popular tourist areas should pay particular attention to their surroundings and always follow the instructions of police and emergency response officials.

Disruptions to travel and daily life remain possible across Europe during the holiday season.  Strikes and demonstrations have occurred with greater frequency in recent months.  In November, hoax bomb threats targeted civil aviation in numerous European countries, disrupting flights.  Americans should monitor local news during holiday travel abroad to stay informed about local events or developments that could disrupt transportation or daily life.  We encourage all U.S. citizens abroad to enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) to receive the latest security updates for their destinations.

Actions to Take:

  • Remain alert.

item.title: Security Alert: Threat to Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve in Moscow (October 31, 2026)
item.content:encoded:
Security Alert: Threat to Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve in Moscow

Security Alert: Threat to Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve in Moscow (October 31, 2026)

The U.S. Embassy in Moscow is aware of a credible threat of a mass casualty event TODAY October 31, at the Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve in Moscow at Dolskaya Ulitsa 1, Moscow, Russia 11569. The U.S. government is coordinating with appropriate Russian authorities on a response.

Actions to take:

  • Avoid the Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve location TODAY, October 31, 2026. Avoid the area, stay alert, and avoid crowds.

item.title: Health Alert – U.S. Embassy Moscow, Russia (October 6, 2026)
item.content:encoded:
Health Alert – U.S. Embassy Moscow, Russia (October 6, 2026)

Location: Irkutsk, Russia

 

Event: The U.S. Embassy is aware of press reports from the Irkutsk region of suspected pneumonic plague resulting in the death of an individual and of associated quarantine measures in, and closures of, hospitals in Irkutsk.  We continue to track the situation closely.  The U.S. government has limited ability to help U.S. citizens in Russia, especially outside of Moscow.  U.S. government personnel may face additional restrictions for personal and official travel to specific regions due to health and security concerns.

 

The State Department’s Level 4 Travel Advisory (Do Not Travel) for Russia remains in place and states U.S. citizens currently in Russia should depart immediately.  U.S. citizens planning travel to Russia are again strongly advised not to travel to Russia due to risk of wrongful detention and security concerns.

 

Actions to Take:

  • U.S. citizens in the area should follow the guidance of local health authorities, avoid affected facilities, and seek medical care promptly if they develop fever or respiratory symptoms.

item.title: Routine Message: Travel and Communication Disruptions, May 8-9, 2025
item.content:encoded:
Routine Message: Travel and Communication Disruptions, May 8-9, 2025

The U.S. Embassy in Moscow is tracking news of major flight disruptions at airports in the Moscow region due to increased drone activity ahead of the Victory Day holiday on May 9.  Passengers should contact their airline for information on their flight status.

Road closures and transportation services in Moscow may be affected due to the Victory Day parade – U.S. citizens are encouraged to monitor local media.

According to Russian telecom providers, from May 8 to 9 there may be restrictions on the operation of mobile internet in the Moscow region.

At this time, U.S. citizens are advised to not travel to Russia – more information on the State Department’s Level 4 Travel Advisory (Do Not Travel) can be found on travel.state.gov.

Actions to Take:

  • Do not travel to Russia
